name: SWERVE
source: Sandia Winged Energetic Re-entry Vehicle (SWERVE). Three flights 1979-1985 from the Kauai Test Facility on STRYPI boosters; flight 3 reentered near Johnston Island (~1,180 km). Spherically blunted 5.25-deg half-angle cone, 'a little over 100 in' long (~2.6 m), with small wings/elevons for lift and control, Mach 2-14 maneuvering. Nose-tip/heat-shield ablative. Flight-3 maneuver (Williamson, AIAA 92-3989, Fig. 20): ~-10 deg AoA push-over at 20 s/Mach 12, +10-15 deg pull-ups, ~4 deg control deflection; all flight data (Figs 20/23/24) end at ~160 s. (The AHW conical glide body is described as 'SWERVE with improved TPS'.)
notes: GEOMETRY sourced: 5.25-deg sphere-cone, nose_radius from published R_n/R_base=0.07 (R_base=L*tan(5.25)~0.238 m -> R_n~0.0167 m). base diameter 0.476 m is the CONE base; the ~0.61 m (2 ft) factsheet 'diameter' includes the wings. MASS ~450 kg (program-class figure; SWERVE and the AHW glide body are both ~450 kg). beta=37,100 kg/m2 = m/(Cd*A) holding the geometry-fixed Cd*A=0.0121 m2 (Cd~0.068 on the 0.178 m2 cone base, a realistic sharp-5.25-deg-cone hypersonic value); it scales with mass, so if mass is revised, rescale beta to keep Cd*A constant. L/D 0.6 is a representative airframe value reflecting the 'small wings' and the modest lift of the maneuvering flight-3 record (Williamson Fig. 20) -- NOT the AHW glide body's higher 1.8. guidance=damped_glide models the maneuvering pull-up/push-over phugoid; the flight-3 loft (Kauai->Johnston, ~1,180 km, ~160 s, Mach ~12) and the exact Fig-20 AoA schedule are flown via the pitch program at run time, not baked into this RV. tps_material=carbon_ablator is the ORIGINAL ablative heat shield; the SWERVE->AHW claim is airframe reuse with an improved shield and higher glide L/D for AHW's much longer range -- AHW differs in TPS, glide L/D, and booster (STARS), not in basic airframe class.
